To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a generic source-code instrumentation component that is configurable via a simple XML-based description file, and that this component is able to instrument a number of different aspects of a given source code.

(1) the basic constructs for source-code instrumentation are (1a) a list of routines to be instrumented, (1b) the instrumentation points, and (1c) a list of instrumentation actions, (2) the instrumentation component is able to handle all of the above constructs, and (3) the instrumentation component can be used for various instrumentation scenarios.

(1) a generic source-code instrumentation component can be realized with only a few, well-defined constructs, and (2) the resulting component is flexible and extensible enough to be used in a number of different contexts.
